fields.description: What the segment billed: the sum of its calculation HEADERS (CI_BSEG_CALC.CALC_AMT). Not the calc lines: lines are itemisation and some clients itemise selectively (Newark: most headers carry no lines), so a line sum undercounts there. See "Itemized Charge Amount" for what the lines cover.
fields.label: Billed Amount

fields.description: The part of "Billed Amount" the calc LINES itemise. Equals "Billed Amount" at a fully-itemising client (Ellensburg); partial where itemisation is selective (Newark). The charge-basis split columns partition THIS figure, to the cent.
fields.label: Itemized Charge Amount

fields.description: The part of "Billed Amount" priced on metered consumption (calc lines with a consumption-class unit and no SQI). THIS is the amount that pairs with "Billed Usage". Caveat: clients that tier consumption through SQI multipliers (ellensburg water) price that revenue as Service Quantity instead.
fields.label: Consumption Charge Amount

fields.description: The part of "Billed Amount" priced on metered demand (kW-class unit, no SQI). Pairs with "Billed Demand".
fields.label: Demand Charge Amount

fields.description: The part of "Billed Amount" priced on a DERIVED service quantity -- daily charges (SQI=DAYS averaging ~29 days), tier multipliers, ERU-based charges. 60% of ellensburg revenue. Not a usage charge even though tiered consumption can sit here.
fields.label: Service Quantity Charge Amount

fields.description: The part of "Billed Amount" priced on nothing -- no unit, no service quantity. Deposits, connection fees inside rated bills.
fields.label: Flat Charge Amount

fields.description: Charges on a unit the uom_class seed does not classify. Should be zero; non-zero means the seed needs a row for a client-configured unit.

rpt_bill_segment.label: Bill Segment

premade_reports.description: Billed revenue is FROZEN segments only. Unfrozen segments are still in flight and cancelled ones were reversed; counting either inflates the total. Not every billed line is revenue either: a payment arrangement is billed but only reschedules debt, so it is split out here rather than silently dropped.
premade_reports.title: What revenue was billed, by service agreement type?

premade_reports.description: Payment arrangements, cash deposits, write-offs, loans and non-billed budgets all put money on a bill without earning any. A payment arrangement reschedules debt that was already billed on another agreement, so counting it as revenue books the same money twice; a deposit is the customer's own money, held as security and refundable. This is the amount a revenue report has to exclude, and the reason it excludes it.
premade_reports.title: How much of what we bill is not revenue?

premade_reports.description: The charge basis split is what tells you whether a rate is volumetric or fixed. It is also the split that goes wrong first when a rate is reconfigured.
premade_reports.title: How does a bill split between consumption, demand, service quantity and flat charges?

premade_reports.description: An estimated bill is a read that did not arrive. A rising rate here is a metering problem showing up as a billing number.
premade_reports.title: How much billing is running on estimates?

premade_reports.description: Every rebill is a bill the utility got wrong the first time. The cancel reason is where the pattern is.
premade_reports.title: How much is being rebilled, and why?

premade_reports.description: The top of the distribution is where billing errors surface first, and where a high-bill complaint is about to come from.
premade_reports.title: Which bill segments are the largest?

premade_reports.description: A segment priced far from every other segment on the same rate is either a proration, a rate change mid-period, or a mistake. All three are worth seeing.
premade_reports.title: Where is the price per unit furthest from its rate's norm?

premade_reports.description: The headline meter-to-cash KPI. Every cancelled and rebilled segment is a bill the utility got wrong and had to redo, and the industry target is above 95% right first time.
premade_reports.title: Billing accuracy rate — what share of bills were not rebilled?

premade_reports.description: Estimated bills generate disputes, and disputes generate calls. A rising estimation rate is an AMI reliability problem arriving as a customer-service cost.
premade_reports.title: Estimation rate — how much revenue is billed on estimates?

premade_reports.description: Cycle is how the billing calendar is actually organised. A cycle whose revenue moves without its customer count moving is a rate or a read problem.
premade_reports.title: What does each bill cycle bring in?

premade_reports.description: Billed usage should be derivable from the reads. A gap means a correction, an override or an estimate — and the customer will notice before the utility does.
premade_reports.title: Where does billed usage disagree with the meter reads behind it?

premade_reports.description: A zero bill is usually a missing read; a negative one is a credit the customer will ring about. Neither should appear without a reason attached.
premade_reports.title: Which bills came out zero or negative?

premade_reports.description: High consumption is a leak, a theft, a faulty meter or a genuinely large customer. Comparing within a rate schedule is what separates the fourth from the first three.
premade_reports.title: Which premises consumed far more than others on the same rate?
